note: 2022 statewide swings (R two-party share, 2022 race minus pres 2020), counties weighted by households; race = state x office, so a county with both a Senate and a governor race enters once per race. exposure_share_within is the R-squared of swing on exposure with race fixed effects, as a share of within-race variance; exposure_share_total is the same explained variance as a share of total variance. pa_slopes are unweighted OLS slopes of swing on exposure e (vote points per unit of e) over the 67 Pennsylvania counties, the line drawn through the dots; pa_slopes_hh weights counties by households.

kept_2026.method: Provisional, from the 2026 price build of 2026-10-19 (state shocks, shocks-0.1.0) with the open 2026 post-window (5 of 21 days; pre-window 21 days); the metro layer is rebuilt in memory with the project's interim rule set (post-window threshold 3 days instead of the registered 10), because the stored sub-state table is empty for 2026. Rows and weights are the 2026 analysis frame on the registered race list (Alaska excluded): county x race, weight = 2024 two-party presidential votes of the county divided by the number of races in its state. Burden B = E x g, with E the commute-and-vehicles exposure and g the county price change. State level: recentered burden B~ = E x (state shock minus its PADD-group mean). Metro level: B~ = E x [(state shock minus its PADD-group mean) + (cluster mean of u minus the mean over clusters in the same state x CBSA-type stratum)], with u the county's metro price change minus its state's; counties outside a covered metro have u = 0. Kept share = weighted within-race variance of B~ divided by weighted within-race variance of B (fb26.models.validate.diagnostics). Price variance shares: across counties, weighted by 2024 two-party presidential votes, g = regional mean (PADD-group mean of state shocks) + state deviation (state shock minus regional mean) + metro deviation (u, zero outside a covered metro); each share is Cov(part, g)/Var(g), so the three sum to 1 (the covariance between parts is split evenly). var_ratio gives Var(part)/Var(g), which need not sum to 1. 2022 check: same kept-share code on the 2022 validation frame.
